synopsis: EMC means electronics must operate amid electrical noise without disturbing other equipment; ISO 16001:2017 requires EMC to ISO 13766 for object detection systems on earth-moving machines [f13021, f2414, f15254]. Field evidence includes variable-frequency-drive nuisance shutdowns documented in 2010, cross-zone interference reported in 2017, and interference involving dust monitors, computers, survey lasers and steel-braided water lines [f3371, f3372, f3373]. The booklet identifies EMC and multi-radar/lidar interference as simulation blind spots, so complete-machine EMC remains a physical-test requirement; MOSH includes EMC in its TRL4 laboratory phase [f5100, f13030, f13031, f493, f5595]. Acceptance criteria must address electromagnetic false triggers, and simultaneous sensor-suite mounting must be tested when it changes electromagnetic or optical behaviour [f13032, f5511]. The skeptic's review rates site-system interoperability and radar interference Medium to High risk and recommends ISO/TS 21815-2 interface tests and radio-frequency coexistence tests; an on-road example illustrates the concern but is reported through a secondary summary [f11076, f11078, f11255].
